subject: science
passage: Common vampire bats must feed on blood almost every night; an adult that fails to feed for two or three nights in a row may starve. Bats that have fed successfully often regurgitate part of their meal to roostmates that have not, and because roosts frequently contain relatives, many biologists have explained this generosity through kin selection: by helping a relative survive, a bat promotes the survival of genes the two share.
passage_b: Behavioral ecologist Tavita Fonoti does not deny that bats favor their kin, but she doubts that kinship is the whole story. In captive colonies whose members' relationships were known, bats regularly fed unrelated roostmates, and whether a bat had previously received food from a particular partner predicted its willingness to feed that partner at least as well as kinship did. Such patterns, Fonoti argues, suggest that long-term reciprocal partnerships, not merely shared ancestry, sustain the behavior.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the explanation in Text 1?

choices.A: By rejecting it, on the grounds that bats share food with unrelated roostmates far more than with kin
choices.B: By accepting it, since food sharing among relatives promotes the survival of the genes they share
choices.C: By arguing that the danger of starvation, rather than kinship or partnership, explains the sharing
choices.D: By granting that kinship plays a role while contending that it cannot fully account for the sharing

explanation.why: Text 1 explains food sharing through kin selection. Fonoti "does not deny that bats favor their kin" but "doubts that kinship is the whole story," because bats fed unrelated partners and past help predicted sharing "at least as well as kinship did." She therefore accepts kinship as a factor while adding reciprocal partnerships.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Fonoti does not reject kin selection, and Text 2 never says bats share with non-relatives more often than with relatives; it says past help predicted sharing "at least as well as" kinship.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Fonoti accepts that kinship matters but argues it is not "the whole story," so she would not simply accept the explanation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 does not treat the risk of starvation as a rival explanation; it adds reciprocity to kinship.
explanation.D: Correct. Fonoti grants that bats favor their kin but argues that reciprocal partnerships also help sustain food sharing.
